analysis.title: Beyond AI: The Power of Humanoids and Automation
key_insights: UBS CIO says AI advances are doubling every seven months, versus 18-24 months for Moore's Law processing power, setting off 'AI in motion' across humanoid robotics, ADAS, robotaxis, aerospace, agriculture, smart glasses and medicine.
Vision-language-action (VLA) models convert sensory input and natural-language instructions directly into motor actions. UBS calls this a transformative shift for robotics and ADAS.
Ageing populations, shrinking workforces and reshoring (high labor cost, labor scarcity, anti-immigration sentiment) are creating labor gaps. UBS expects this to accelerate adoption of embodied AI.

UBS advises broad exposure to embodied-AI verticals: humanoid robots, ADAS, robotaxis, and niche segments in industrial automation, agritech, smart glasses, robotic surgery and drones. It describes this as a complementary source of alpha not captured by existing TRIO strategies.
List changes: ASML, PDD Holdings and Toyota Motor were added. Alibaba Group, Intuitive Surgical and Johnson & Johnson were removed. The NVIDIA portfolio weight was raised from 6.5% to 7.5%.

TAM estimates: USD 402bn for humanoids and automation within a decade (11% CAGR), USD 40bn global humanoid market by 2035, USD 88bn ADAS (including FSD) by 2035, USD 40bn robotaxi, and USD 134bn aggregate for agritech, robotic surgery, EVTOL and smart glasses (23% CAGR).

Alibaba was removed because UBS sees better opportunities in PDD. PDD was added for its mind share in the value-for-money segment and Temu's overseas expansion. UBS flags short-term volatility because the company is in an investment phase.
Intuitive Surgical and Johnson & Johnson were removed for lack of near-term catalysts. UBS says removal does not indicate a negative view.
ASML was added for its lithography position (EUV monopoly), pricing power and AI-driven demand. UBS flags the risk of an uneven revenue recovery and capacity-scaling execution risk.
NVIDIA's weight rises to 7.5%. UBS expects strong Data Center growth but says results and the share price may be choppy, and that large-scale GenAI monetization has not yet been seen.

Oracle: UBS sees USD 17 EPS by FY30 excluding OpenAI (a 23% CAGR from May 2025), with shares at under 11x that estimate. Management targets USD 250bn revenue and USD 21 EPS. Shares have been pressured by OpenAI exposure and rising leverage.
Salesforce is trading at its lowest forward multiples in over a decade amid the AI disintermediation narrative, and has a record USD 50bn buyback authorization.
Samsung: HBM siphoning DRAM capacity and disciplined supply are tightening memory. HBM4 working samples are with hyperscalers, and UBS expects full-scale HBM4 shipments in 2026.
Panasonic's AI data center battery backup unit business contributes around 30% of operating profit and is expected to be the key earnings driver.
Toyota was added on a P/BV at its long-term average, a dividend yield above 3.0%, a 10% operating margin, and a planned large share buyback in 1H26 following an expected TOB of a subsidiary.
Siemens plans to spin off 30% of Siemens Healthineers to shareholders, leaving a stake below 20% in the medium term. UBS says the stock trades at a discount to its model.
Effective 1 November 2026, UBS CIO no longer rates or ranks equities. 'CIO Selected' is a designation, not a rating, and portfolio weights do not express conviction or relative merit.

Deere: UBS says autonomous-agriculture revenue could rise four to five times by the end of the decade, and the AI-driven share of revenues could reach 5-10%. It sees agricultural demand near a cyclical low.
Yaskawa is developing humanoid actuators and acquired Tokyo Robotics in July 2025. UBS sees recovering semiconductor servo demand and Japanese policy support for AI robots as catalysts.

sector_views.rationale: UBS sees a new cycle upturn in global automation, with labor gaps and reshoring driving demand for embodied AI.
AI compute demand, HBM memory tightness, EUV lithography and advanced-node foundry growth support multiple selected names.
Selected software names (MSFT, ORCL, CRM, ADSK) are favored on AI exposure and valuations, including Salesforce at its lowest forward multiples in over a decade.
Deere is a leader in autonomous agriculture, but UBS says agricultural demand is nearing a cyclical low and a prolonged soft period could delay recovery.

earnings_insights: Oracle: UBS estimates USD 17 EPS by FY30 excluding the OpenAI agreement (a 23% CAGR from May 2025). Management's long-term targets are USD 250bn revenue and USD 21 EPS. These are forecasts, not reported figures.
ABB: UBS expects double-digit organic sales growth this year and close to double-digit growth in 2027/28, with double-digit annual profit growth in 2026-28 (UBS estimates).
Keyence: UBS expects double-digit profit growth next fiscal year as margins turn around (UBS estimate).
Toyota: UBS expects earnings to recover in FY26 as the tariff impact fades. It cites a 10% operating margin and a planned large buyback in 1H26.
TSMC: AI-related revenue is projected by management and UBS to grow at a mid- to high-50% CAGR between 2024 and 2029.
risk_factors: A global economic downturn or industrial demand slowdown would hit ABB, Siemens, Schneider, Keyence, THK and Yaskawa.
Hyperscaler and data center capex could prove uneven or slow, which would affect NVDA, Schneider, MSFT, AMZN and ASML.
Yen appreciation is a risk for Japanese names (Keyence, THK, Toyota, Yaskawa, Daifuku).
OpenAI exposure and rising leverage are risks for Oracle.
AI disintermediation and competition could erode Salesforce's pricing power.
Agricultural demand could stay depressed longer than expected, delaying Deere's recovery.
US policy deterioration and price wars could hurt Toyota.
Delays in HBM approval at key customers and smartphone demand destruction could hurt Samsung.
geopolitical: US reshoring and anti-immigration sentiment are cited as raising labor costs and scarcity, and so as raising demand for automation.
US tariffs and trade conflicts are cited as risks for Keyence, Toyota, THK and TSMC, and as a headwind to Toyota earnings that should fade.
Chinese humanoid and AI robot development is covered through Tencent's Tairo platform, Chinese local robot makers competing with Yaskawa, and PDD's Temu overseas expansion.
